fake.h: Thief in {} crawls through a museum vent to steal a 1984 iPhone prototype, sells it for $60
fake.tell: The iPhone didn't exist until 2007, so no 1984 prototype could be stolen.

fake.h: Smugglers in {} hide 14 rhino tusks inside hollowed-out watermelons at a border market
fake.tell: Rhinos have horns, not tusks.

fake.h: Fraudster in {} sells 212 tickets to a rooftop concert on 29 February 2027, then vanishes
fake.tell: 2027 is not a leap year, so there is no 29 February.

fake.h: Bus driver in {} takes 38 commuters 410 km to see his mother, a 3-hour trip at 60 km/h
fake.tell: Three hours at 60 km/h covers only 180 km, not 410.

fake.h: Bootlegger in {} is jailed for selling single malt whisky distilled from grapes to 31 pubs
fake.tell: Single malt whisky is made from malted barley; grape spirit is brandy.

fake.h: Mosaic under a vineyard in {} shows Roman diners at a banquet eating potatoes and chilli peppers
fake.tell: Potatoes and chillies came from the Americas, unknown in Roman times.

fake.h: Woman, 23, in {} is jailed for running a pyramid scheme from her parents' garage in 1994
fake.tell: A 23-year-old today wasn't born in 1994.

fake.h: Burglar in {} drags a stolen 137-kg safe across a lake frozen 3 cm thick, and the ice holds
fake.tell: Ice 3 cm thick can't carry a man dragging a heavy safe.

fake.h: Undertaker in {} says a dead man's beard grew 6 cm in the 11 days before his funeral
fake.tell: Hair and nails do not keep growing after death; the skin just retracts.

fake.h: A farmer in {} plows up a 10th-century Viking helmet with both bull horns still attached
fake.tell: Vikings did not wear horned helmets in battle.

fake.h: Pupils open a 1979 school time capsule in {} and find a USB stick holding 212 photos
fake.tell: USB sticks did not exist until around 2000.

fake.h: Love letter mailed in 1957 at age 19 is returned to its 93-year-old writer in {}, 66 years late
fake.tell: Someone aged 19 in 1957 would be about 85 after 66 years, not 93.

fake.h: Man in {} proposes with a ring baked into a fortune cookie from a Beijing bakery open since 1650
fake.tell: Fortune cookies are a Californian-Japanese invention, not an old Chinese tradition.

fake.h: Two cyclists, both 80, end a 63-day ride across the Sahara, the world's largest desert, in {}
fake.tell: Antarctica, not the Sahara, is the largest desert on Earth.

fake.h: Clockmaker in {} finds a Post-it note dated 1923 inside a grandfather clock, listing 14 groceries
fake.tell: Post-it notes were not invented until the late 1970s.

fake.h: George Washington's wooden teeth, carved from oak, sell for $212,000 at an auction in {}
fake.tell: Washington's dentures were made of ivory, metal and human teeth, never wood.

fake.h: From his roof in {}, an engineer, 67, photographs the Moon's far side with a 23-cm telescope
fake.tell: The Moon is tidally locked, so its far side never faces Earth.

fake.h: Man, 31, in {} is charged with cashing his late father's pension for 38 years by forgery
fake.tell: A 31-year-old can't have collected a pension for 38 years.

fake.h: Archivists in {} find a 1604 sailor's diary written in ballpoint pen, listing 41 days at sea
fake.tell: Ballpoint pens weren't invented until the 1930s.

fake.h: Lost tourists in {} survive 3 days in the desert by drinking water from a camel's hump
fake.tell: Camel humps store fat, not water.

fake.h: Brothers in {} go to court over 47 years of knuckle-cracking at dinner, blamed for arthritis
fake.tell: Cracking knuckles doesn't cause arthritis.

fake.h: Cyclist in {} delivers a wedding cake 640 km away in 5 hours, and it arrives still warm
fake.tell: That needs an average of 128 km/h on a bicycle.

fake.h: Pub in {} hosts the 30th real birthday of a man born on 29 February, who is turning 75
fake.tell: Leap-day birthdays come every four years, so 75 gives about 18, not 30.

fake.h: Retiree in {} pays 41,300 dollars for a rock Apollo 8 astronauts supposedly picked up on the Moon
fake.tell: Apollo 8 only orbited the Moon; it never landed.

fake.h: A zip fastener is found sewn into the door flap of Napoleon's 1805 field tent, restored in {}
fake.tell: Zip fasteners were not invented until the 1890s and 1910s, long after 1805.

fake.h: Cathedral panes from 1320 have sagged 3 cm as the glass slowly flowed, glaziers in {} find
fake.tell: Glass is not a slow-flowing liquid at room temperature; old panes are uneven from how they were made.

fake.h: In {}, a convent cooks 40 guests a tomato sauce from a recipe book sealed in a wall in 1370
fake.tell: Tomatoes reached Europe from the Americas only after 1492, so no 1370 recipe could use them.

fake.h: Lighthouse keeper, 54, retires in {} after climbing his 212 steps twice daily for 61 years
fake.tell: A 54-year-old cannot have worked for 61 years.

fake.h: Orchestra in {} premieres a lost Mozart piece from 1788, scored for four saxophones
fake.tell: The saxophone was invented in the 1840s, decades after Mozart died in 1791.

fake.h: Undertakers in {} exhume a coffin after 9 years and find the dead man's beard grown 27 cm
fake.tell: Hair and nails do not keep growing after death; the skin shrinks and makes them look longer.

fake.h: Metal detectorist in {} digs up a 10th-century Viking helmet with both horns intact
fake.tell: Vikings did not wear horned helmets.

fake.h: Distillery in {} crushes 22 tonnes of cactus a week to make a 4,870-peso tequila
fake.tell: Tequila is distilled from blue agave, which is not a cactus.

fake.h: Grandmother, 81, and her grandson row 1,450 km of coast in {} in 6 days, averaging 4 km/h
fake.tell: At 4 km/h, even rowing nonstop for 6 days covers only about 576 km.

fake.h: Sculptor in {} hides a 21-cm lift in the boots of a Napoleon statue to mask his short height
fake.tell: Napoleon was of average height for his time; his shortness is a myth.

fake.h: Dog walker in {} finds a horned Viking helmet from 940 AD in a peat bog and wears it to the pub
fake.tell: Vikings didn't wear horned helmets; that image is a 19th-century invention.

fake.h: Escaped inmate in {} walks 82 km home in 5 hours to make his mother's birthday dinner
fake.tell: Walking 82 km in 5 hours means over 16 km/h, far beyond walking pace.

fake.h: Caretaker, 31, in {} admits stealing the same school bell every Friday for 38 years
fake.tell: A 31-year-old can't have been stealing for 38 years.

fake.h: Con artist in {} sells 61 tickets to a street party on 29 February 2027; 40 buyers turn up
fake.tell: 2027 is not a leap year, so 29 February 2027 doesn't exist.

fake.h: Tour operator in {} sells 47 guests polar-bear-spotting cruises to Antarctica, then disappears
fake.tell: Polar bears live in the Arctic; there are none in Antarctica.

fake.h: Restaurateur in {} flies in a Beijing baker to teach staff the ancient craft of fortune cookies
fake.tell: Fortune cookies aren't an ancient Chinese tradition; they were popularised in early 20th-century California.

fake.h: Physicists in {} drain 212 bathtubs to prove Earth's spin decides which way water swirls
fake.tell: The Coriolis effect is far too weak to steer water in a bathtub.

fake.h: Under a beet field in {}, a farmer finds a Viking helmet with two curved 30-cm horns
fake.tell: Vikings didn't wear horned helmets; that is a myth.

fake.h: Grandmother, 83, drives a lawn mower 1,900 km across {} at 8 km/h, finishing in 6 days
fake.tell: At 8 km/h, 6 days nonstop is only about 1,150 km, not 1,900.

fake.h: Two fishermen adrift 19 days off {} say they stayed alive by drinking only seawater
fake.tell: Drinking seawater dehydrates and kills; nobody survives 19 days on it alone.

fake.h: The 1310 monastery feast recreated in {} for 90 guests includes potato dumplings and turkey
fake.tell: Potatoes and turkey came from the Americas and reached Europe after 1492.

pol.h: City council seat in {} goes to a candidate after a coin flip breaks an election tie
pol.clue: city council + coin-flip tiebreak; a small city northwest of the Mayo Clinic
